payload.title: Invictibellatrix
payload.wikitext: {{Short description|Genus of theropod dinosaur}} {{Speciesbox | fossil_range = [[Early Cretaceous]], {{fossilrange|Barremian|Barremian|[[Barremian]]}} | image = Invictibellatrix amberina (holotype, NHMUK PV R6775).png | image_caption = Photographs (left) and line drawings (right) of the holotype specimen | display_parents = 2 | genus = Invictibellatrix | parent_authority = Morrison et al., [[2026 in archosaur paleontology|2026]] | species = amberina | authority = Morrison et al., 2026 }} '''''Invictibellatrix''''' ([[Latin]]: "unconquered warrior") is an [[extinct]] genus of [[megaraptora]]n theropod dinosaur known from the [[Early Cretaceous]] ([[Barremian]] age) [[Wessex Formation]] of England. The genus contains a [[Monotypic taxon|single species]], '''''Invictibellatrix amberina''''', known from a single braincase. == Discovery and naming == The ''Invictibellatrix'' fossil material was discovered in outcrops of the [[Wessex Formation]] on the [[Isle of Wight]], United Kingdom. The specimen is housed in the [[Natural History Museum, London|Natural History Museum]] in [[London]], where it is permanently [[Accession number (cultural property)|accessioned]] as specimen NHMUK PV R 6775. It was sold to the museum in May 1924 by the widow of the collector [[Reginald Hooley|Reginald Walter Hooley]]. It consists of an isolated [[braincase]] (part of the skull that houses the brain). Prior to the formal naming of ''Invictibellatrix'', the fossil material was reported in a [[Academic conference|conference]] [[Abstract (summary)|abstract]] in 2024. In 2026, Cassius Morrison and colleagues [[Species description|described]] ''Invictibellatrix amberina'' as a new genus and species of megaraptoran theropod based on these fossil remains, designating NHMUK PV R 6775 as the [[holotype]] specimen. == Description == [[File:Invictibellatrix amberina.png|thumb|left|Speculative [[life restoration]]]] ''Invictibellatrix'' is estimated to have a body mass between {{cvt|200–300|kg}} and a body length of around {{cvt|4|m}}. Three [[autapomorphies]] (unique derived traits) were recognized. On each side of the parabasisphenoíd in front of the ''recessus tympanicus anterior'', a small ''recessus basipterygoideus'' is present. The crest on the back of the skull is lightly transversely compressed and has an hourglass profile. On the crest, distinctive, lightly curved depressions are present on the midline. ==Phylogeny== In their 2026 description of ''Invictibellatrix'', Morrison and colleagues tested the affinities of this taxon using multiple phylogenetic matrices and analytical techniques. These generally recovered ''Invictibellatrix'' as a derived member of the megaraptoran family Megaraptoridae, which is otherwise almost entirely restricted to the Late Cretaceous of Gondwana. A close relationship with ''[[Murusraptor]]''—one of the few megaraptorans that preserves braincase material—was consistently recovered. Using a fossilized birth–death analysis (a method that incorporates the stratigraphic ranges of taxa studied) of the Aranciaga Rolando et al. (2022) dataset, ''Invictibellatrix'' was instead recovered in a more [[Basal (phylogenetics)|basal]] position within Megaraptora, outside of the Megaraptoridae, a position much more consistent with its early occurrence.
